visible_constraints: Confirmation dialog states: 'A $100.00 reimbursement will be sent to the original payment method.'
Cancel order, Request refund, and Request price adjustment controls were all co-visible before cancellation and all disappear together once the order is canceled
observed_changes: Status banner appeared: 'Order canceled and reimbursement issued.'
Order activity gained entry 'Order canceled' with 'Reimbursement issued to original payment method' and amount $100.00
'Request price adjustment' button disappeared and Price protection region text changed from 'Eligible' to 'Unavailable'
Order actions region text changed to 'This order has no actions requiring your attention.' / 'No further actions are available for this order.'

roles.name: anonymous
roles.note: No authentication cookies, bearer tokens, or CSRF headers were present on any request in the recording (GET /api/order or POST /api/order/cancel). Only a single unauthenticated session context was observed; this is not reported as a vulnerability per scope.json (authentication_required is not set to true).

observed_ui_rules.statement: Once an order is canceled, the Cancel order and Request refund controls disappear and are no longer available.

inference.text: The order-cancellation workflow intends the cancel and refund-request actions to become permanently unavailable once cancellation completes.

observed_ui_rules.statement: Price protection becomes unavailable to the customer while another order request (cancellation) is active.

facts.text: paragraph : The price of this item has dropped since your purchase.
paragraph : Price protection is not available while another order request is active.

inference.text: The client displays price protection as 'Unavailable' once cancellation is active, even though the server-side priceProtection.status field is not observed to change (remains 'eligible' in both GET /api/order and POST /api/order/cancel responses). This is an unverified hypothesis worth testing server-side: the API may still accept a price-adjustment request after cancellation despite the UI hiding the control.

conflicting_action_pairs.rule: Cancel order, Request refund, and Request price adjustment were all simultaneously visible/enabled; the resource can only end up in one terminal disposition (canceled, refunded, or price-adjusted), so concurrently invoking more than one should not both take effect.

actions.name: request_refund
actions.note: UI exposes a 'Request refund' button and order.refund{status,requestedAmount,completedAmount} fields, but no matching request was recorded and no such path exists in endpoint_catalog.json. Endpoint deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed from the button label.

actions.name: request_price_adjustment
actions.note: UI exposes a 'Request price adjustment' button and order.priceProtection.adjustmentAmount, but no matching request was recorded and no such path exists in endpoint_catalog.json. Endpoint deliberately left unresolved rather than guessed from the button label.

critical_endpoints.why: Cancels the order and unconditionally issues a $100.00 reimbursement to the original payment method with no request body (no order/state validation inputs from the client), an irreversible financial state transition. Agent inference (unverified): because the request body is empty, the endpoint likely derives all state from server-side session/order context; it is worth testing whether it can be replayed, invoked without the confirmation dialog ever being shown (FORCED_BROWSING), or invoked again after the order is already canceled (REPLAY_ATTACK) to see if a duplicate $100.00 reimbursement can be triggered. The co-visible 'Request refund' and 'Request price adjustment' UI affordances (see conflicting_action_pairs) have no resolvable endpoint in endpoint_catalog.json and are not targeted here.
